title: U.S. Senate · Iowa

context.text: Incumbent Joni Ernst (R), first elected in 2014, is not running for re-election. Ernst endorsed Hinson on January 10, 2026.

Hinson defeated Jim Carlin 74.0%–25.7% in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary. Turek defeated Zach Wahls 62.6%–37.3% in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary. Laehn advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on May 2, 2026.

As of June 30, 2026, Turek had raised $3.91 million and Hinson had raised $6.75 million in disbursements/receipts as reported by Ballotpedia; Laehn's campaign reported $54,429 in contributions and $46,095 in expenditures as of the same period.

candidates.name: Josh Turek
candidates.currentRole: Member, Iowa House of Representatives, District 20 (since 2023)

summary.text: Josh Turek is the Democratic nominee. A Council Bluffs native and four-time Paralympian on the U.S. wheelchair basketball team, he worked for a mobility-equipment company before winning a state House seat in 2022 by six votes. He is running for the open seat of retiring Sen. Joni Ernst (R), emphasizing health care, public education and costs for middle-class families.

background.text: Born April 12, 1979, in Council Bluffs, Iowa; born with spina bifida, which he and his campaign link to his father's Agent Orange exposure in Vietnam, and underwent 21 surgeries by age 12.

Graduated from Abraham Lincoln High School in Council Bluffs, earned a bachelor's degree from Southwest Minnesota State University in 2002 (where he played wheelchair basketball), and later earned an MBA from DeVry University.

Played wheelchair basketball professionally in Europe for nearly two decades and on the U.S. national team in four Paralympic Games, winning a bronze medal (2012) and gold medals (2016, 2020), according to Wikipedia; his campaign website describes him as a two-time Paralympic gold medalist.

Worked at a wheelchair and mobility-equipment company (NuMotion, per Wikipedia), helping patients obtain mobility devices, and served as volunteer director of the Ryan Martin Foundation, which provides sports opportunities for children with disabilities, according to his campaign website.

Elected to Iowa House District 20 in 2022, winning by six votes out of about 6,800 cast after a recount requested by his opponent in a district that voted Republican in every presidential election since 1968; he took office January 9, 2023, as the legislature's first permanently disabled member, according to Wikipedia.

Re-elected in 2024 with 52.5% of the vote; serves on the House Health and Human Services Committee and the Health Policy Oversight Committee, and led bipartisan legislation (the "Work without Worry" program) removing Medicaid income limits for employed Iowans with disabilities, according to Wikipedia.
Announced his U.S. Senate candidacy on August 12, 2025, and won the Democratic primary over state Sen. Zach Wahls.

Has been inducted into the Athletic Halls of Fame at Abraham Lincoln High School and Southwest Minnesota State University and the National Wheelchair Basketball Association Hall of Fame; lives in Council Bluffs with his wife, Jarolin, who works in health care, according to his campaign website.

priorities.text: Cut taxes for the middle class and close loopholes for billionaires and large corporations; impose a federal ban on price gouging on food; raise the minimum wage and tie future raises to inflation.
Restore full funding for Medicaid, protect and expand the Affordable Care Act, and cap prescription drug costs.
Ban Wall Street private equity firms from purchasing single-family homes and farmland, and simplify permitting so more affordable housing can be built.

positions.summary: Turek says women should make decisions about their reproductive health care, not politicians, and sponsored legislation in the Iowa House to repeal Iowa's near-total abortion ban.
Turek's platform calls for raising the federal minimum wage and tying future increases to inflation.
Turek's platform calls for closing tax loopholes for billionaires and large corporations and strengthening Social Security by requiring billionaires to pay their fair share.
Turek's platform calls for restoring full Medicaid funding, expanding the Affordable Care Act, and introducing a public health insurance option.
Turek's platform calls for ending the current tariffs, citing their effect on Iowa farms.
positions.quote: End the chaotic tariffs that are sending farms toward a 1980s-style farm crisis.

record.text: Sponsored legislation in the Iowa House to strengthen the veterans homestead tax credit.
Sponsored legislation to make it easier for Iowans with disabilities to repair wheelchairs and mobility devices.
Sponsored legislation to cap insulin costs at $25/month and to expand access to dental services under Medicaid.
Sponsored legislation to cut taxes for first-time homebuyers and to limit private equity purchases of Iowa homes.
Served on the Iowa House Human Resources, Natural Resources, State Government, and Veterans Affairs committees (2025-2026); ranking member of the House Veterans Affairs Committee (2023-2024).

candidates.name: Ashley Hinson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2 Republican primary; endorsed by retiring Sen. Joni Ernst

summary.text: Ashley Hinson is the Republican nominee and the U.S. Representative for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2020. A former KCRG-TV anchor and reporter in Cedar Rapids, she served in the Iowa House from 2017 before running for Congress. She is running for the open seat of retiring Sen. Joni Ernst (R) and has Ernst's endorsement.

background.text: Born in Des Moines, Iowa, in 1983; lives in Marion, Iowa. Wikipedia reports she graduated from Valley High School in West Des Moines.
Earned a B.A. in broadcast journalism from the University of Southern California.

Worked as a news anchor and reporter at KCRG-TV in Cedar Rapids for more than a decade, winning two regional Emmy awards and recognition as an RTDNA Health Reporting Fellow, according to her House website.
Has served with organizations including the Cedar Rapids Metro Economic Alliance, March of Dimes and Junior Achievement of Eastern Iowa, according to Ballotpedia.

Elected to the Iowa House of Representatives (District 67, Linn County) in 2016 and re-elected in 2018, serving from 2017 until she took her U.S. House seat; she chaired the Transportation Committee and served on Judiciary and Public Safety, according to Wikipedia.

Won the 2020 Republican primary and then the general election for Iowa's 1st District over Rep. Abby Finkenauer (51.2% to 48.6%); after redistricting she ran in and won the 2nd District in 2022, and was re-elected in 2024.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and, per Ballotpedia, the Ethics Committee in the 2025-2026 Congress.
Her House website says she and her husband, Matt, are raising two sons in Marion and that she plays violin at Antioch Christian Church.

priorities.text: Lower taxes for working families, help more families become homeowners through a proposed First Home Savings Opportunity Act, and prevent institutional investors from buying up single-family homes.
Secure the U.S.-Mexico border, enforce immigration law, and combat fentanyl trafficking.
Lower prescription drug costs, strengthen rural health care, and support family farms and biofuels including year-round E15.

positions.summary: Hinson's platform calls for securing the southern border, enforcing immigration laws, and deporting criminal immigrants who are in the country without legal permission.
Hinson's House issues page says she is pro-life and that taxpayer dollars should not fund abortion providers or abortions.
positions.quote: I am pro-life and pro-family and will remain a strong and consistent voice for mothers and their children. We must protect the unborn and stand up for the sanctity of life.

record.text: Serves on the House Appropriations Committee (subcommittees on Agriculture-FDA, Homeland Security, and Financial Services-General Government), the Committee on Ethics, and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Thomas Laehn
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on May 2, 2026

summary.text: Thomas Laehn is the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in Iowa. An attorney with graduate degrees from Louisiana State University, he was elected Greene County Attorney in 2018 and says he was the first Libertarian elected to a partisan office in Iowa. He says he is running on ending eminent domain abuse, stopping undeclared wars and reducing the national debt.

background.text: Graduated from Allison-Bristow High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Drake University, a master's degree and Ph.D. from Louisiana State University, and a law degree from the University of Iowa.

Works as an attorney; was elected Greene County Attorney, the county's local prosecutor, in 2018 and is finishing his second term, and says he was the first Libertarian to hold an elective partisan office in Iowa, per his Ballotpedia survey response.
Lives in Jefferson, Iowa, with his wife, Susan, and their two children, according to his Ballotpedia survey response.
Advanced as the Libertarian Party's nominee for U.S. Senate from the party's state convention on May 2, 2026.

priorities.quote: As a U.S. Senator, I will work to pass legislation prohibiting private companies from harnessing the coercive power of the state to seize property for commercial gain, ending eminent domain abuse in our nation.

priorities.text: Stop wars begun without congressional consent and bring U.S. troops home.
priorities.quote: block foolish wars declared by presidents without the consent of Congress

priorities.text: Fight the national debt, including voting against funding measures that increase it.
priorities.quote: I will vote against every funding measure that would result in an increase in our national debt, except in cases of extreme national emergency.

positions.summary: In his Ballotpedia survey, says he would work to block wars declared by presidents without the consent of Congress.
positions.quote: block foolish wars declared by presidents without the consent of Congress

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities come from Laehn's 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His campaign site (thomaslaehn.com) still carries his 2022 county attorney re-election content and has no Senate issue pages. Press coverage (Iowa Public Radio, KCRG) paraphrases his views on abortion, tariffs and marijuana but does not quote him directly on the guide's issue statements, so none were added.

researchNotes: Turek's platform positions and record items are sourced from his campaign website and Ballotpedia's summary of his Iowa House record; the Iowa House bill-sponsorship claims are as described by Ballotpedia's race summary, not independently verified against bill text. Laehn's research is minimal: no active 2026 Senate campaign website or issue statements were found; the site available under his name promotes an earlier county-attorney campaign, so his positions are omitted rather than inferred. Biography gaps: Laehn's biography rests on his Ballotpedia survey (no news profile or 2026 campaign site found), and Hinson's and Turek's birth, early-life and Iowa House details partly rely on Wikipedia where no official page states them.
